title: Two Indians Quarantined in Netherlands After MV Hondius Outbreak
excerpt: Embassy of India confirms both crew members are healthy and asymptomatic as global hantavirus case count climbs to 11.
body:
Two Indian crew members aboard the Dutch polar cruise ship MV Hondius have been evacuated to the Netherlands for quarantine, the Embassy of India in Madrid confirmed on May 10 — the first direct Indian involvement in a fast-moving hantavirus outbreak that has now killed three people.

**What happened:**
The MV Hondius, operated by Oceanwide Expeditions, departed Ushuaia, Argentina on April 1, 2026, carrying roughly 150 passengers and crew from 23 nationalities. A passenger died onboard on April 11. The vessel anchored off Spain's Canary Islands on May 10, where all remaining passengers disembarked under WHO and Spanish authority protocols. The Embassy confirmed that the two Indians — both serving as crew members — are 'healthy and asymptomatic' and are being quarantined in the Netherlands in line with international health safety procedures. Indian Ambassador to Spain Jayant N Khobragade is personally monitoring the situation.

**Why this matters:**
The strain onboard is the Andes virus, the *only* known hantavirus variant with documented human-to-human transmission, carrying a case fatality ratio of up to 38% in this outbreak. The US CDC has classified the event a 'level 3' emergency response. Separately, twelve Dutch hospital staff entered preventative quarantine after a protocol breach while treating an evacuee. India's ICMR-National Institute of Virology has urged calm, stating the cases among Indian nationals appear to be isolated imports with no evidence of community spread inside India. The WHO concurs, assessing the global population risk as low.

**What to watch:**
Monitor whether the two Indian crew members test positive during their quarantine window, and whether WHO updates its risk assessment as the MV Hondius sails back to Rotterdam with approximately 30 crew still aboard.

nri_angle: Indian-Americans with family members working on international cruise lines or planning polar voyages should be aware that India's government is actively tracking this outbreak and that isolation protocols — not the virus itself — currently pose the most immediate disruption to Indian nationals abroad.
